response_text:
1. (Currently amended) An aircraft weapons control system comprising: a weapons stores processor panel for receiving input signals from a weapons input; a weapons interface for receiving fire signals from the weapons stores processor panel to control firing of aircraft weapons; and a flight management system in communication with the weapons stores processor panel and the weapons interface, the flight management system providing control signals to the weapons interface; wherein the weapons stores processor panel implements safety interlocks to prevent or enable firing of the aircraft weapons; __wherein the weapons stores processor panel receives the input signals from the weapons input independent of the flight management system and processes the input signals prior to communicating with the weapons interface__.

2. (Original) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 wherein: the weapons interface includes a first weapons interface to a first weapon and a second weapons interface to a second weapon, the first weapon and the second weapon being of different types.

3. (Original) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 2 wherein: the weapons interface includes a third weapons interface to a third weapon and a fourth weapons interface to a fourth weapon, the third weapon and the fourth weapon being of different types.

4. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 wherein: the [[weapons processor]] __weapons stores processor__ panel communicates with the weapons interface using a MIL-STD-1760 standard __and a MIL-STD-1553 avionics interface bus__.

5. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 further comprising: a laser pointer __selectively powered__ coupled to the weapons processor panel __via a dedicated laser arm control__.

6. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 further comprising: a data concentrator unit that conditions outputs from the flight management system for display on a multi-function display __and that operates independently of the weapons stores processor panel__.

7. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 further comprising: a control panel on the [[weapons processor]] __weapons stores processor__ panel, the control panel including a master arm switch for selecting a master arm position, a safe position and an off position.

8. (Original) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 7 wherein: when the master arm switch is in the master arm position, the weapons stores processor panel provides power to a weapons interface controller and the weapons stores processor panel enables generation of the fire signals.

9. (Original) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 7 wherein: when the master arm switch is in the safe position, the weapons stores processor panel provides power to a weapons interface controller and the weapons stores processor panel prevents generation of the fire signals.

10. (Original) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 7 wherein: when the master arm switch is in the off position, the weapons stores processor panel disables power to a weapons interface controller and the weapons stores processor panel prevents generation of the fire signals.

11. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 7 wherein: the control panel also includes a laser arm switch for __selectively powering__ a laser pointer through the weapons stores processor panel __independent of the master arm switch position__.

12. (Original) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 further comprising: a control panel on the weapons stores processor panel, the control panel including a override switch for having a weight-on-wheels (WOW) position and a manual override position.

13. (Original) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 12 wherein: when the override switch is in the manual override position, the weapons stores processor panel commands the weapons interface directly, without reliance on the flight management system.

14. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 further comprising: a control panel on the weapons stores processor panel, the control panel including a weapons select switch which designates a weapon to fire, the weapons select switch including an off position in which the weapons stores processor panel disables fire signals [[the]] __to the__ weapons interface.

15. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 wherein: the weapons stores processor panel provides display information __generated from the weapons stores processor panel's independent processing__ for a helmet mounted display, control display unit, and a multifunction function display __without intermediary processing by the flight management system__.

16. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 wherein: the weapons stores processor panel provides data __directly__ for a weapons bus controller to implement firing of weapons __based on commands generated by the weapons stores processor panel independent of the flight management system__.

17. (Currently amended) A vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL) rotary-wing aircraft comprising: an aircraft mounted weapon; and an aircraft weapons control system, the aircraft weapons control system including: a weapons stores processor panel for receiving input signals from a weapons input; a weapons interface for receiving fire signals from the weapons stores processor panel to control firing of the aircraft weapon; and a flight management system in communication with the weapons stores processor panel and the weapons interface, the flight management system providing control signals to the weapons interface; wherein the weapons stores processor panel implements safety interlocks to prevent or enable firing of the aircraft weapon; __wherein the weapons stores processor panel receives the input signals from the weapons input independent of the flight management system and processes the input signals prior to communicating with the weapons interface__.

18. (Currently amended) The rotary-wing aircraft of claim 17 further comprising: a laser pointer __selectively powered__ coupled to the weapons stores processor panel __via a dedicated laser arm control__.

19. (Original) The rotary-wing aircraft of claim 17 further comprising: a control panel on the weapons stores processor panel, the control panel including a master arm switch for selecting a master arm position, a safe position and an off position.

20. (Original) The rotary-wing aircraft of claim 19 wherein: when the master arm switch is in the master arm position, the weapons stores processor panel provides power to a weapons interface controller and the weapons processor panel enables generation of the fire signals.

21. (Original) The rotary-wing aircraft of claim 19 wherein: when the master arm switch is in the safe position, the weapons stores processor panel provides power to a weapons interface controller and the weapons stores processor panel prevents generation of the fire signals.

22. (Original) The rotary-wing aircraft of claim 19 wherein: when the master arm switch is in the off position, the weapons stores processor panel disables power to a weapons interface controller and the weapons stores processor panel prevents generation of the fire signals.

23. (Currently amended) The rotary-wing aircraft of claim of claim 19 wherein: the control panel also includes a laser arm switch for __selectively powering__ a laser pointer through the weapons stores processor panel __independent of the master arm switch position__.

24. (Original) The rotary-wing aircraft of claim of claim 17 further comprising: a control panel on the weapons stores processor panel, the control panel including an override switch for having a weight-on-wheels (WOW) position and a manual override position.

25. (Original) The rotary-wing aircraft of claim 24 wherein: when the override switch is in the manual override position, the weapons stores processor panel commands the weapons interface directly, without reliance on the flight management system.

26. (Currently amended) The rotary-wing aircraft of claim 17 further comprising: a control panel on the weapons stores processor panel, the control panel including a weapons select switch which designates a weapon to fire in a manual over-ride mode, the weapons select switch including an off position in which the weapons stores processor panel disables fire signals [[the]] __to the__ weapons interface.
